set_aside.subject: Storage of admission verdicts
set_aside.text: K-05 says “Admission is one recorded verdict”, but K-10’s exhaustive list of records the kernel stores omits admission verdicts: “contracts, implementations, trial evidence, activations, bindings, flow versions, approvals and grants, runs and traces”.
set_aside.question: Is an admission verdict a stored kernel record, and if so what existing record category contains it; otherwise what does “recorded” mean?
options: Treat the verdict as part of trial evidence
Do not persist the verdict and derive it when needed
set_aside.default_guess: Store a distinct admission-verdict record linked to the implementation and the corpus it covered.

witness.initial: An implementation has passed every case and has been activated; the process is then restarted.
events: The kernel admits the implementation and records the verdict.
An operator restarts the kernel process.
An agent asks to roll the slot back to that implementation.
outcomes: The persisted verdict proves that the implementation is admitted over the current corpus, so rollback succeeds.
No admission-verdict record is permitted by K-10, so the kernel must derive or recreate a verdict, or refuse rollback.

set_aside.subject: How the recorded admission verdict is produced
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus” does not say whether admission executes every case afresh, aggregates previously recorded trial evidence, or uses some other observation; the separate actions “try an implementation” and “admit and activate” permit both readings.
set_aside.question: What observations must the kernel use to produce the recorded admission verdict when an implementation is submitted?
options: Execute every active case once during admission
Reuse the latest stored trial evidence for every active case
Require explicit successful trial evidence and then record its aggregate
Execute cases repeatedly according to a specified rule
set_aside.default_guess: Execute every active case once during the admission triggered by submission and aggregate those executions.

witness.initial: The corpus contains one case, and the implementation has successful trial evidence for it but can obtain chance through an undetected mechanism allowed by K-02.
events: An agent explicitly tries the implementation and that trial passes.
The agent submits the same implementation for admission.
A fresh execution of the case would fail.
outcomes: Admission uses the recorded successful trial evidence and admits and activates the implementation.
Admission executes the corpus afresh, records failure, and refuses activation.

set_aside.subject: Identity and replacement of an admission verdict
set_aside.text: “Admission is one recorded verdict” does not identify what the verdict is keyed by or whether a later submission may replace it, while equal implementation content returns the existing implementation and trial cases may later be added to the contract version’s corpus.
set_aside.question: For an immutable implementation, is there one permanent verdict, one verdict per corpus revision, or a replaceable verdict per submission; and how can an existing implementation obtain a verdict over a corpus that grew after its prior verdict?
options: One permanent verdict per implementation; corpus growth permanently makes it ineligible for current-corpus use
One immutable verdict per implementation and corpus revision
One current verdict per implementation that is replaced on each submission
Multiple admission-attempt verdicts, with a rule selecting the operative one
set_aside.default_guess: Record an immutable verdict per implementation and exact corpus revision; resubmitting an existing implementation evaluates the current corpus and adds a new verdict.

witness.initial: Implementation I is admitted and active over corpus containing case A.
events: An author adds case B to the same contract version.
Case B would pass for I.
The author submits code equal to I, so the authoring action returns the existing implementation.
Later an agent requests rollback to I after another implementation has become active.
outcomes: Resubmission evaluates I against corpus {A,B}, records a new admitted verdict, and rollback to I is allowed.
I retains only its original verdict over {A}; equal content creates no new implementation or verdict, so rollback is refused as lacking an admitted verdict over the current corpus.
witness.observer: The author and the later rollback requester

set_aside.subject: Repeatability of admission for nondeterministic implementations
set_aside.text: Replacing “a deterministic verdict” with “one recorded verdict” leaves open whether the same implementation against the unchanged corpus may be admitted again after a refusal and whether a later, different observed result supersedes the earlier verdict.
set_aside.question: May admission be retried for the same implementation and unchanged corpus, and if repeated executions disagree, which recorded verdict controls activation and rollback?
options: The first verdict is final for that implementation and corpus
Every submission creates a new verdict and the latest controls
Retries are allowed only after the corpus or implementation changes
All recorded attempts remain authoritative, so any recorded failure prevents admission
set_aside.default_guess: Permit a new admission attempt on resubmission and let its newly recorded verdict control activation, while retaining earlier attempts as history.

witness.initial: The corpus is unchanged and an implementation uses an undetected source of chance permitted by K-02.
events: The agent submits the implementation; its case fails and admission is refused.
The agent submits identical content again; the case now passes.
outcomes: The second recorded verdict is admitted and the implementation activates.
The first recorded verdict is the one verdict for that implementation and corpus, so the second submission returns the existing refusal and cannot activate it.
